content: 1. Citalopram and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 4. Erythromycin stearate decreases the activation of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing clopidogrel’s bioactivation. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 6. Cobicistat and erythromycin stearate increase each other’s levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg daily. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors. If necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency. Colchicine is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 9. Conivaptan increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while cortisone decreases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Crizotinib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and cyclosporine increases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darifenacin increases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Darunavir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and dasatinib increases erythromycin stearate levels. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Degarelix and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 19. Desflurane and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 20. Desipramine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 22. DHEA increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and diltiazem increases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Consider alternatives to erythromycin in patients receiving diltiazem. 26. Dofetilide and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 27. Donepezil and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 28. Doxepin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and dronedarone increases erythromycin stearate levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 30. Droperidol and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases edoxaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Dose adjustments may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 32. Efavirenz decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Reduce eluxadoline dose to 75 mg twice daily if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half. 38. Erythromycin stearate increases enoxaparin effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 39. Erythromycin stearate and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 40. Enzalutamide decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Epinephrine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 42. Racemic epinephrine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 43. Erdafitinib increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases ergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 45. Eribulin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. If necessary, monitor ECG. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases erlotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 47. Escitalopram increases erythromycin stearate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 48. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Erythromycin stearate increases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases esterified estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases estropipate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 53. Erythromycin stearate increases etonogestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases erythromycin stearate levels. This combination is contraindicated. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). This combination is contraindicated. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases felodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 57. Erythromycin stearate increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl dose as needed. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases fesoterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 59. Fexinidazole increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 60. Fingolimod and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 61. Erythromycin stearate increases fludrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 62. Fluphenazine and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 63. Erythromycin stearate increases fondaparinux effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 64. Erythromycin stearate and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 65. Erythromycin stearate increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and fosamprenavir increases erythromycin stearate levels. This combination is contraindicated.
